Drift Recovery Update

An update on the ~$295.4M taken from Drift users on 1 April, and where recovery efforts stand.

Drift Foundation will continue pursuing efforts to track, trace, and recover stolen funds. Recovered funds, whether they come back through a freeze, bounty, or through law enforcement, shall be directed into the DFX recovery pool.

Mandiant, zeroShadow, and SEAL 911 were brought in to investigate and trace the funds. Mandiant identified the attacker as UNC6862, a North Korean threat group. Since April, zeroShadow has tracked the stolen funds, including the laundering that began in July, and has shared its findings with law enforcement.

—

Where the funds are

The stolen funds were bridged to Ethereum, ~130,259 ETH across four wallets. Three of those four wallets have not moved and currently hold 107,165 ETH. On 23 July, one of the wallets sent about 23,094 ETH into Tornado Cash.
